newsitem.title: USA: Ferro to cut 1,200 jobs, close 30 plants.
newsitem.headline: Ferro to cut 1,200 jobs, close 30 plants.

text.p: Ferro Corp., a major producer of coatings, colours, ceramics, chemicals and plastics, said Monday it expects to cut 1,200 jobs as it closes about 30 of its 80 manufacturing plants worldwide in a restructuring.
The company, which has 6,900 employees worldwide, said the cutbacks would take place mainly outside of the United States.

Ferro will take an after-tax charge of about $100 million in the second quarter to pay for the three-year restructuring, which aims to boost revenues by focusing on marketing and technology, instead of managing multiple facilities, it said.
The charge -- of $153 million before taxes -- includes costs to write off and mark down assets and severance charges.
The plan is expected to cost about $38 million in cash over the three years. When completed, it should improve operating profit by more than $30 million a year, Ferro said.
"We need to concentrate on opportunities for growth, which we see primarily in Asia-Pacific and the United States," said Hector Ortino, president and chief operating officer.
"To maximize those opportunities, we need to reduce a great deal of the complexity and level of management attention required to manage a large number of plants."
The facilities to be closed have annual capital expenditures of about $15 million, Ferro said.
The Cleveland-based company said it aims to increase its gross profit margin to 28 percent by the end of 1999 from 25 percent in 1996 through the restructuring.
Most of the initiatives in the restructuring will be taken in the first two years of the plan, Ortino said.
Ferro's stock rose $2.375 to $33.75 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.
